newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airline AOM loses 140 mln Ffr in 1996.
newsitem.headline: French airline AOM loses 140 mln Ffr in 1996.

text.p: French airline AOM said on Monday that it had lost 140 million francs in 1996 but aimed to turn a profit this year.

It said in a statement that turnover rose 10 percent last year to 3.5 billion francs and passengers increased by 30 percent. It gave no 1995 comparative figures, and officials were not immediately available for comment.

AOM said last year's results reflected a price war in France's air travel industry, higher fuel prices and a rise in the dollar. "The AOM Group...has an objective to return to profit in 1997," it said.

It said it had implemented a more aggressive commercial policy, adjusted routes and mobilised staff to attain this objective. "The first signs of improvement are visible with a 12 percent rise in passenger turnover in 1997," it said.
